pieds-noirs.name: Pieds-Noirs
pieds-noirs.summary: An ethno-cultural group of French and other European descent born in Algeria under French colonial rule from 1830 to 1962, most of whom left for France during or after the Algerian War of Independence.

harissa.name: Harissa
harissa.summary: Tunisian hot chili pepper paste of roasted red peppers, garlic, caraway and other spices, recognized by UNESCO as part of Tunisia's Intangible Cultural Heritage.

tagine.name: Tagine
tagine.summary: A Moroccan stew named for the earthenware pot it is cooked in, whose domed lid traps condensation so the ingredients braise with little added water.

sfax.name: Sfax
sfax.summary: A major Tunisian port city founded in AD 849, now the country's second-largest city, known for phosphate, olive and fishing industries.

chermoula.name: Chermoula
chermoula.summary: A marinade and relish used in Algerian, Libyan, Moroccan and Tunisian cooking, traditionally used to flavor fish, somewhat similar to Latin American chimichurri.

makroudh.name: Makroudh
makroudh.summary: Diamond-shaped Maghrebi cookie made from semolina dough and filled with dates and nuts or almond paste, fried or baked.

medina-quarter.name: Medina quarter
medina-quarter.summary: A general Arabic term for the old, historically walled district of a North African city.

bardo-national-museum-tunis.name: Bardo National Museum
bardo-national-museum-tunis.summary: A museum of arts and North African history in Le Bardo, Tunis, the second-largest museum in Africa, holding one of the world's largest collections of Roman mosaics.

hadrumetum.name: Hadrumetum
hadrumetum.summary: A Phoenician colony that predated Carthage and later became an important city of Roman Africa, now part of Sousse, Tunisia.

dougga.name: Dougga
dougga.summary: A Berber, Punic and Roman settlement in northern Tunisia, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site called the best-preserved small Roman town in North Africa.

utica-tunisia.name: Utica
utica-tunisia.summary: An ancient Phoenician and Carthaginian city near Carthage in modern Tunisia that became an important Roman colony after Carthage's defeat, before its harbour silted up.

hassan-ii-mosque.name: Hassan II Mosque
hassan-ii-mosque.summary: A mosque in Casablanca, Morocco, completed in 1993, the second-largest in Africa, with the world's second-tallest minaret at 210 metres and room for 105,000 worshippers.

mausoleum-of-mohammed-v.name: Mausoleum of Mohammed V
mausoleum-of-mohammed-v.summary: A mausoleum in Rabat, Morocco, holding the tombs of King Mohammed V and his sons, King Hassan II and Prince Abdallah.

institut-du-monde-arabe.name: Institut du Monde arabe
institut-du-monde-arabe.summary: An organization founded in Paris in 1980 by France and 18 Arab countries to research and promote Arab culture, art and knowledge, housed in a building with a museum and library.

gabriel-camps.name: Gabriel Camps
gabriel-camps.summary: French archaeologist and social anthropologist (1927–2002) who founded the Encyclopédie berbère and is considered a leading scholar of Berber history.

encyclop-die-berb-re.name: Encyclopédie Berbère
encyclop-die-berb-re.summary: French-language encyclopaedia on Berber peoples and culture, launched in 1984 under UNESCO and first edited by Gabriel Camps.

salafist-group-for-preaching-and-combat.name: GSPC
salafist-group-for-preaching-and-combat.summary: An Algerian Islamist militant group founded in 1998 during the Algerian Civil War, which later pledged support to al-Qaeda and became al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb in 2007.
salafist-group-for-preaching-and-combat.source_title: Salafist Group for Preaching and Combat

al-qaeda-in-the-islamic-maghreb.name: Al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb (AQIM)
al-qaeda-in-the-islamic-maghreb.summary: An al-Qaeda-linked Islamist militant organization active in North Africa's Maghreb and Sahel regions, known for kidnapping for ransom, that grew out of an Algerian insurgent group.

algerian-civil-war.name: Algerian Civil War
algerian-civil-war.summary: A civil war fought from 1992 to 2002 between the Algerian government and Islamist rebel groups, known in Algeria as the Black Decade, with total fatalities estimated at 40,000 to 50,000.

operation-juniper-shield.name: Operation Enduring Freedom – Trans Sahara
operation-juniper-shield.summary: US-led military operation, later renamed Operation Juniper Shield, that works with partner nations across the Sahara and Sahel on counterterrorism and anti-trafficking as part of the Global War on Terrorism, begun in 2007.

ben-guerdane.name: Ben Guerdane
ben-guerdane.summary: A coastal town in southeastern Tunisia near the border with Libya.

attack-on-mers-el-k-bir.name: Attack on Mers-el-Kébir
attack-on-mers-el-k-bir.summary: 1940 British naval attack on French ships at their base near Oran, Algeria, meant to keep the fleet from falling into German hands after France's defeat.

vichy-france.name: Vichy France
vichy-france.summary: The French state headed by Marshal Pétain from 1940 to 1944, formed after Germany's victory over France and based in the town of Vichy in the unoccupied 'free zone.'

french-west-africa.name: French West Africa
french-west-africa.summary: A federation of eight French colonial territories in West Africa, eight times the size of mainland France, that existed from 1895 to 1958 with its capital at Dakar.

ansar-al-sharia-tunisia.name: Ansar al-Sharia (Tunisia)
ansar-al-sharia-tunisia.summary: A Salafi Jihadist group that operated in Tunisia with roughly 10,000 members in 2013, listed as a terrorist organization by several governments and the UN after pledging allegiance to Al-Qaeda.

jebel-ech-chambi.name: Jebel ech Chambi
jebel-ech-chambi.summary: The highest mountain in Tunisia, at 1,544 metres, standing above the city of Kasserine near the Algeria–Tunisia border.

libyan-civil-war-2014-2020.name: Second Libyan Civil War
libyan-civil-war-2014-2020.summary: A multilateral civil war fought in Libya from 2014 to 2020, mainly between the House of Representatives and the Government of National Accord.

assia-djebar.name: Assia Djebar
assia-djebar.summary: Algerian novelist, translator and filmmaker (1936–2015) known for feminist and anti-colonial writing; in 2005 she became the first Maghreb writer elected to the Académie Française.

acad-mie-fran-aise.name: Académie Française
acad-mie-fran-aise.summary: France's principal authority on the French language, established in 1635, made up of forty lifetime members who publish an official dictionary.

neustadt-international-prize-for-literat.name: Neustadt International Prize for Literature
neustadt-international-prize-for-literat.summary: A biennial literary award sponsored by the University of Oklahoma since 1970, often called the 'American Nobel' for its prestige and overlap with Nobel laureates.

marie-louise-belarbi.name: Marie-Louise Belarbi
marie-louise-belarbi.summary: French-Moroccan bookseller and publisher who spent most of her life in Morocco, where she founded the bookstore Carrefour des Livres and published writers such as Françoise Sagan and Tahar Ben Jelloun.

abdelkebir-khatibi.name: Abdelkebir Khatibi
abdelkebir-khatibi.summary: Moroccan literary critic, novelist, philosopher and poet (1938–2009) who challenged the social and political norms of the Maghreb region in his writing.

plural-maghreb.name: Plural Maghreb
plural-maghreb.summary: A 1983 book of six critical essays by Abdelkebir Khatibi presenting the Maghreb as 'a horizon of thought' and a model for plurality and alternative thinking.

cherchell.name: Cherchell
cherchell.summary: A town on Algeria's Mediterranean coast, once the Roman colony of Iol/Caesarea and capital of the kingdoms of Numidia and Mauretania.

tahar-ben-jelloun.name: Tahar Ben Jelloun
tahar-ben-jelloun.summary: Moroccan writer born in 1944 who rose to fame with his 1985 novel The Sand Child and has been nominated for the Nobel Prize in Literature.

driss-chra-bi.name: Driss Chraïbi
driss-chra-bi.summary: A Moroccan novelist (1926–2007), based partly in Paris, whose often semi-autobiographical works explored colonialism, culture clashes and the treatment of women.

abdellah-ta-a.name: Abdellah Taïa
abdellah-ta-a.summary: Moroccan writer and filmmaker, born 1973, writing in French from Paris since 1999, who in 2006 claimed to be the first openly gay Arab writer.

ahmed-marzouki.name: Ahmed Marzouki
ahmed-marzouki.summary: Former Moroccan military officer forcibly disappeared after the failed 1971 coup and imprisoned at the secret Tazmamart detention centre from 1973 to 1991, who wrote a memoir about the experience.

les-temps-modernes.name: Les Temps modernes
les-temps-modernes.summary: A French literary magazine founded after World War II by Jean-Paul Sartre with Simone de Beauvoir, published from 1945 until it ceased in 2019.

dorothy-blair.name: Dorothy Blair
dorothy-blair.summary: English scholar and translator of Francophone African literature, born Dorothy Sara Greene in 1913 and died in 1998.

ditions-julliard.name: Éditions Julliard
ditions-julliard.summary: A French publishing house founded in 1942, known for discovering literary talents such as Françoise Sagan and Jean d'Ormesson.

fran-oise-sagan.name: Françoise Sagan
fran-oise-sagan.summary: French playwright, novelist and screenwriter (1935–2004) known for stories of wealthy, disillusioned characters; her best-known novel, Bonjour Tristesse, was written as a teenager.

bonjour-tristesse.name: Bonjour Tristesse
bonjour-tristesse.summary: A 1954 novel by French writer Françoise Sagan, published when she was only 18, that became an overnight sensation; its title comes from a Paul Éluard poem.

jacques-berque.name: Jacques Berque
jacques-berque.summary: French scholar of Islam and sociologist (1910–1995) at the Collège de France, specializing in the decolonisation of Algeria and Morocco and Arab cultural heritage.

edward-said.name: Edward Said
edward-said.summary: Palestinian and American academic and literary critic (1935–2003) best known for his 1978 book Orientalism, a founding text of post-colonial studies.

ibn-khaldun.name: Ibn Khaldun
ibn-khaldun.summary: An Arab Tunisian scholar and historian (1332–1406), best known for the Muqaddimah, a foundational work in historiography, sociology and economics.

maghreb-virtual-science-library.name: Maghreb Virtual Science Library
maghreb-virtual-science-library.summary: A project giving researchers in the Maghreb full-text access to science and engineering journals and databases, funded by the U.S. Department of State.

crdf-global.name: CRDF Global
crdf-global.summary: A US nonprofit, authorized by Congress in 1992 and established in 1995, that promotes international scientific and technical collaboration through grants and training.

university-of-nouakchott-al-aasriya.name: University of Nouakchott Al Aasriya
university-of-nouakchott-al-aasriya.summary: A university in Nouakchott, the capital of Mauritania.

medina-of-sousse.name: Medina of Sousse
medina-of-sousse.summary: A UNESCO World Heritage walled old town in Sousse, Tunisia, listed in 1988 as an example of early Islamic architecture in the Maghreb, including a kasbah and the Great Mosque of Sousse.

representative-concentration-pathway.name: RCP 8.5
representative-concentration-pathway.summary: One of the original Representative Concentration Pathways adopted by the IPCC for climate modeling, representing a high-emissions scenario with a large rise in radiative forcing by 2100.

orange-tunisia.name: Orange Tunisia
orange-tunisia.summary: Tunisian telecom company that became the country's leading 3G mobile operator after gaining a license in 2010; the state seized part of its ownership in 2011 over fraud allegations.

research4life.name: Research4Life
research4life.summary: A platform giving researchers in over 200 low- and middle-income countries free or low-cost access to academic journals, books and databases since 2002.

jstor.name: JSTOR
jstor.summary: A digital library founded in 1994 that provides full-text search of nearly 2,000 academic journals, plus books and other sources.

alawi-dynasty.name: Alawi dynasty
alawi-dynasty.summary: Morocco's ruling royal family since the 17th century, claiming descent from the Prophet Muhammad, who ruled as sultans until the 1912 French protectorate and became kings after independence in 1956.

muhammad-v-of-morocco.name: Muhammad V
muhammad-v-of-morocco.summary: Ruler of Morocco from 1927 to 1961, reigning first as sultan and later as its first king, who led the country to independence from France and Spain and is credited with protecting Morocco's Jewish population during World War II.

pan-arabism.name: Pan-Arabism
pan-arabism.summary: An ideology from the late 19th century calling for the unification of all Arab countries into one nation, tied to Arab nationalism and opposition to Western involvement.

ugo-vetere.name: Ugo Vetere
ugo-vetere.summary: An Italian Communist Party politician (1924–2013) who served as mayor of Rome from 1981 to 1985 and signed a symbolic 1985 treaty ending the ancient Punic Wars.

chedli-klibi.name: Chedli Klibi
chedli-klibi.summary: Tunisian politician (1925–2020) who served as Secretary-General of the Arab League, the only non-Egyptian to hold that post.

moktar-ould-daddah.name: Moktar Ould Daddah
moktar-ould-daddah.summary: Mauritania's first prime minister and first president after independence from France, ruling from 1957 until a 1978 military coup; he built an authoritarian one-party state.

tablighi-jamaat.name: Tablighi Jamaat
tablighi-jamaat.summary: An international Islamic revivalist movement founded in 1926 in British India, urging Muslims toward stricter religious observance through short preaching tours.

mohamed-khouna-ould-haidalla.name: Mohamed Khouna Ould Haidalla
mohamed-khouna-ould-haidalla.summary: Mauritanian military officer, born 1940, who served as head of state from 1980 to 1984 and later ran unsuccessfully for president in 2003 and 2007.

maaouya-ould-sid-ahmed-taya.name: Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya
maaouya-ould-sid-ahmed-taya.summary: Mauritanian military officer and politician, born 1941, who served as President from 1984 to 2005 and earlier as Prime Minister, pursuing Arab nationalist policies.

rabat-sal-airport.name: Rabat-Salé Airport
rabat-sal-airport.summary: An international airport near Salé serving Rabat, Morocco's capital, also home to the Royal Moroccan Air Force's First Air Base.

habib-bourguiba.name: Habib Bourguiba
habib-bourguiba.summary: Tunisian politician who led the country to independence from France and served as its first president from 1957 to 1987, earning the title 'Supreme Combatant.'

albert-bessis.name: Albert Bessis
albert-bessis.summary: Tunisian politician (1885–1972) who directed urban planning and housing after independence and served in parliament until 1969.

grand-synagogue-of-tunis.name: Grand Synagogue of Tunis
grand-synagogue-of-tunis.summary: A Jewish synagogue in Tunis, Tunisia, also called the Temple of Osiris, located on Avenue de la Liberté.

treaty-of-fes.name: Treaty of Fes
treaty-of-fes.summary: Signed under duress by Sultan Abd al-Hafid in March 1912, it established the French protectorate over Morocco and sparked violent backlash known as the Intifada of Fes.

andr-servier.name: André Servier
andr-servier.summary: A historian in French Algeria at the start of the 20th century.

french-algeria.name: French Algeria
french-algeria.summary: France's colonial rule over Algeria from the 1830 conquest of Algiers until Algerian independence in 1962; scholars estimate 500,000 to 1,000,000 Algerians died from it by 1875.

jacques-derrida.name: Jacques Derrida
jacques-derrida.summary: French philosopher (1930–2004) who developed deconstruction and became a major figure in post-structuralism, influencing fields from literature to law worldwide.

louis-bertrand-novelist.name: Louis Bertrand
louis-bertrand-novelist.summary: A French novelist, historian and essayist (1866–1941), elected to the Académie française in 1925.

coll-ge-de-france.name: Collège de France
coll-ge-de-france.summary: A prestigious higher education and research institution in Paris, founded in 1530 by Francis I of France.

maghrebi-jews.name: Maghrebi Jews
maghrebi-jews.summary: A Jewish diaspora group with roots in the Maghreb (Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya) going back over 2,000 years, once numbering around 1.8 million and now the second-largest Jewish diaspora.

algerian-war.name: Algerian War
algerian-war.summary: An armed conflict from 1954 to 1962 between France and the Algerian National Liberation Front that won Algeria its independence and caused the fall of France's Fourth Republic.

cr-mieux-decree.name: Crémieux Decree
cr-mieux-decree.summary: An 1870 law granting French citizenship to Algeria's Jewish population while excluding Muslim Arabs and Berbers, deepening divisions that shaped the 1954–1962 Algerian War.

christopher-silver-music-historian.name: Christopher Silver
christopher-silver-music-historian.summary: American academic, curator and writer based in Canada, known for research on the 20th-century cultural history of Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia, especially Jewish-Muslim relations through music.

maliki-school.name: Maliki school
maliki-school.summary: One of the four major Sunni Islamic legal schools, founded by Malik ibn Anas in the 8th century, predominant across North and West Africa and parts of the Gulf.

arab-barometer.name: Arab Barometer
arab-barometer.summary: A nonpartisan research network that has run public opinion surveys across the Arab world since 2006, run with Princeton and Michigan universities and regional partners.

bah-faith.name: Baháʼí Faith
bah-faith.summary: A religion founded by Baháʼu'lláh in 19th-century Iran teaching the unity of all religions and people, with 7 to 8 million followers worldwide today.
